Wish by Chopard is a Oriental Vanilla fragrance for women. Wish was launched in 1997. The nose behind this fragrance is Nathalie Lorson. Top notes are Coconut, Strawberry, Gooseberry, Black locust, Pear, Black Currant, Brazilian Rosewood, Honeysuckle, Yuzu and Orange Blossom; middle notes are Honey, Milk, Orchid, Heliotrope, Violet, Osmanthus, Magnolia, Jasmine and Lily-of-the-Valley; base notes are Caramel, Vanilla, Patchouli, Toffee, Incense, Sandalwood, Amber and Tonka Bean.

Wish by Chopard is an Oriental Vanilla fragrance for women. Wish was launched in 1999. The nose behind this fragrance is Nathalie Lorson. Top notes are honeysuckle, black locust, orange blossom, coconut, gooseberry, Brazilian rosewood, pear, black currant and yuzu; middle notes are honey, violet, orchid, milk, heliotrope, lily-of-the-valley, jasmine, magnolia and osmanthus; base notes are sandalwood, amber, patchouli, vanilla, caramel, incense, tonka bean and toffee.

gingermojo 05/31/25 06:43

Wish is reminiscent of Angel, Mugler’s original powerhouse patchouli gourmand. In the latter nineties, I remember sampling both of these side by side in a department store. I actually preferred Angel, and so went with that over the Chopard. Fast forward to 2007. I was active duty in the military and a new mother of two. I still owned Angel, but whether due to my body’s new status as a mom, reformulation or both, Angel wasn’t quite scratching the itch it used to. A friend of mine had a bottle of Wish that had turned a peculiar witchy shade of brown. She explained that it happens to Wish after a time because of the rather large amount of natural vanillin in it, that natural vanillin eventually darkens but that it doesn’t affect the scent at all. The last time I had sampled Wish was a decade prior, but I was curious, and I spritzed a little on the back of my hand. Again, whether due to differences in my body or reformulation, I now found myself loving the creek-bottom brown juice in the pretty diamond shaped flacon. Personally, I don’t think the current formulation is 100% the same as it was in the late ‘90’s, but it’s still very much the same …perhaps a bit more sweet? Compared to the current girlish and monumentally sugared and honeyed gourmands of today, Wish smells more mature and womanly, and I love that (of course I love the current ones too!😉)

I still own both, a bottle of Angel that lays down, and a bottle of Wish that turned from light blue to a translucent brown several years ago. On me, I find Angel is spicy/aromatic rather than a full tilt gourmand (by today’s standards of what’s considered gourmand) with the “edible” facets dialed back from how forward they were in the nineties. By comparison, Wish is sweeter and more floral, with incense and patchouli playing very strong supporting roles. There are some subtle overlaps, but in terms of smell, they’re obviously two different fragrances.

If you don’t like powder, incense and patchouli to be strong in your fragrances, trust me, Wish is not for you. As such, for your own sake and for the sake of those around you, Wish should be applied with a light hand! Wish has a very heavily stacked fragrance profile and its strength and longevity in the current formulation are still pretty formidable. This is not a frag I would wear in hot weather! But Wish is perfect in colder weather.

It is nothing like all the perfumes that it is compared to. It is so unique, the notes are blended so beautifully that you cannot pinpoint exactly what you’re smelling at first. The smell on clothes or in the air is completely different from how it smells on the skin. Annemarie 01/10/25 22:55

At first this one reminded me not of Angel (thankfully) but the long and sadly discontinued Badgley Mischka. The latter was loved by some but it was extremely dense and syrupy (but not sugary), really just too much, and therein lay the origins of its demise I think. Presumably BM couldn't market it aggressively enough to reach enough people who could love it.

Wish is not as daring as angel or BM but is more wearable. I'm happiest once Wish sheds some of its fruity notes and settles into its long languid drydown of sweet patchouli. (The patchouli in Angel always reminds me of gasoline).

Strong for the first 20 mins but more manageable after that. Give yourself some time before you leave the house, but after that you'll be fine. I paid $AUD 20 for 30mls. Worth every cent.

With repeated wearings I do get the resemblance to Angel. There IS a touch of candyfloss, in addition to the fruit, in Wish's sweet accord. I maintain that the patchouli is much less aggressive in Wish.

By 1997 Angel was flying off the shelves so this was Chopard's attempt to grab something of that market, I guess. The bottle design is a clear reference to Angel but the juice, which by all accounts used to be blue, is now a peculiar shade of brown.

This is going to sound strange, but this instantly reminded me of my grandfather. It has a very nice, soapy, clean fragrance that reminds me of a more feminine version of the ancient Imperial Leather Aftershave Lotion from Cussons.

I get mostly violet (powdery light floral), osmanthus (milky leather), Brazilian rosewood (spicy wood) and tonka (tobacco almond) from this, and I can't help but think that the reviewer below, who described this as a compliment getter from men, will have experienced this, because the fragrance is inherently comforting, familiar and something that invokes memories in people.

I'm not saying it's a masculine fragrance, because it's very soft and cosy, but I do think this is pretty unisex.

LunaFortuna 01/11/24 03:42

A common theme I see as I scroll through the reviews is people talking about Angel. Angel this, Angel that. People compare it to Angel and talk about how it either smells like Angel or is absolutely nothing like Angel. I think that the comparisons are mostly psychological and due to the fact that Angel and Wish are both blue colored perfumes in similar looking bottles. Had this been in any other perfume bottle, with any other juice color, then I think the comparisons to Angel would be less abundant.

The opening is very different from Angel's. However, the similarity lies in the sense that you can tell that there is an abundant amount of notes in the opening, as well as the dry down, and in the base. The thing is, though, they're all very different notes except for a small select few, such as the patchouli, sandalwood, and the small handful of others. The note composition, aside from the few shared notes, are quite different. For example, the opening of Wish is almost tropical, I would say. The opening is a lot less complex than Angel's. It's woodier, a bit airier, powdery, and there's a tropical freshness from the fruits and florals in the opening. This is a fruity, floral, powdery, and slightly tropical fragrance due to the likes of the coconut and such. I also detect some soapiness in here.

The patchouli dry down is nice and sweet, and in that regard, I could see it being reminiscent of Angel, but so are the plethora of other gourmand patchoulis on the market that dry down to a chocolatey and sweet base. Longevity was decent, projection was decent, but it wasn't an overly heavy fragrance by any means. In my humble opinion, I feel as though I've smelled fragrances far closer to Angel than this is. Angel is my signature scent, and I immediately recognize when a fragrance is Angel-adjacent. Had you blind folded me, never shown me the bottle, or the juice color, then I'd never really think to compare it to Angel due to them being so different. However, because I had already known that the juice and bottles were so similar, I immediately tried to find every little similarity to Angel in here. And yes, don't get me wrong, they are both fruity, floral, and gourmand patchouli fragrances. However, they are by no means siblings. Cousins? Perhaps. If I had to describe it, I'd say that Wish is the younger second cousin of Angel who is quieter and lives somewhere beachy and more tropical.

Although Chopard Wish was launched 26 years ago, I haven't tested it until now. I don't know how often it has been reformulated over the years; my review will focus on the current version.
Let's start with the obvious: TM Angel was such a success that it literally redirected the entire development of the perfume industry 'for her'. Countless other gourmands followed, and we are still suffering the consequences of that trend (well, at least, those among us who are not so keen on gourmands are suffering). Wish is not a carbon copy of Angel, but it is sufficiently similar, with an abundance of vanilla, patchouli, and then foody and fruity notes. The scent is initially strong, but it doesn't last quite as long as Angel, and in direct comparison, I would say that Wish is more powdery.
Bottom line: Wish is a safe buy for those who love fruitchoulies and gourmand fragrances; however, it is not something that I would ever wear, because my preferences are exactly opposite (I love green, woody, musky and floral scents).

rozberry 12/27/22 15:19

I have in my fragrance wardrobe a few scents which I refer to as my "problem perfumes." Wish is one of them.

On one hand I found myself disappointed on my first smell because I had built myself up to expect a dupe of the unwearable-on-my-skin Angel by Mugler. I was hoping that it would work better than Angel does on my skin, as I adore the DNA of Angel but can't wear it. Wish is nothing like Angel for the most part. In fact, it is very similar in a few ways to Euphoria by Calvin Klein.

And that's where the positives start for me - I absolutely ADORE Euphoria, it's easily one of my most favourite scents. The two scents are similar in that they share a sort of berry-orchid top and a creamy-gourmand middle, but the base is where they differ most. Euphoria takes on a deep woodsy scent, while Wish becomes more gourmand and chocolate sweet.

In terms of notes I'm finding that Wish is largely tart berries on the top, and coconut cream vanilla unctuousness the further towards the base it goes. The shared note of orchid with Wish and Euphoria is probably what is selling Wish to me since I love it so much in Euphoria.

I've seen others saying that Wish is drowning in patchouli, and I wish this was the case - but am also glad it's not? I think the overwhelming presence of patchouli in Angel is what stops me from wearing it. I think there's just enough in Wish that it works. It's growing on me very slowly.

So will Wish remain a "problem perfume" for me, or will it takes its place on my fragrance rotation? I can see myself wearing it with shimmering, glittery clothes (although its a shame I didn't get to wear that combo around Christmas time.) I think it would also go well with a curls-down, scarf-on outfit for a day in town. Perhaps not quite sexy enough for date nights, and not seductive enough to make me into a man eater (thank goodness I have Euphoria for those bimbo vibes!)

I have a head cold right now so I am teeming with excitement to smell this properly when my nose isn't completely blocked!!

EDIT about 1 week later:
So my nose is now completely clear again and I have made an interesting discovery:

Spray a little of Wish, you get the Euphoria notes I described.
Spray a LOT of Wish, and THAT'S where the similarities to Angel by Mugler kick in. I'm not sure what changes exactly about the scent when you spray a lot of it - it may just be that there are more molecules and so the scent seems "thicker" but it's tickling a very similar part of my nose as Angel does. I can detect a bit more of that caramel-praline sweetness that Angel has, in place of the tropical fruits I detect in a few spritzes of Wish.

So there's that!

Every time I saw it, the bottle called to me in its own soft siren song - “Don’t you wish you had Wish?” Yes! I said, and now I do. Some perfumes are perfectly themselves, start to finish, from name to bottle to drydown, and Wish is one of them. She is entirely herself, and like the facets in the bottle, she shows different sides on different days. I love her for it. I love the prominent honey, something that I crave in perfume and that thoroughly delights me, and the alcoholic tinge to it here is like Jack and honey. And the coconut! as far from summer as coconut can get, but so beautiful and truly nutty here. Everything else is in the blend and what she chooses to reveal or emphasize of it on a given day. The description and ingredients of Wish are right in my type, but the reality of it is completely different and far from what I usually love, yet I do love it. Wish is a unique gem. I would never have believed that these words would come out of my mouth, because I do so love the power houses and heavy hitters, but I don’t care about the longevity or projection here. While decent, the experience of Wish is more important to me. I’ve not encountered any perfume that affects me this way before. I spray heavily, as is my habit and inclination, and just go with what comes of it. So much comes of it. And the cap atop the very lovely bottle? Shiny, sleek, minimalist, and mechanical, which I really like. The ring is very effective for removing the cap easily. It is also a little like pulling the pin on a grenade, maybe a reminder to be careful what you wish for! As I said, perfectly herself from beginning to end.

Edit: The more often I wear this, the more I love the drydown. It gets sweeter and more floral - the heliotrope and violets really shine. The longevity on well moisturized skin is ridiculous - all day and into the night from morning application. I just love Wish.

Anna Komnene 01/25/21 21:28

Let's try again. I deleted my first review as I've changed my mind on some things. It's true that Angel and Wish share the same DNA ( patchouli+ sweetness) but they're two different scents, each of their own. The main difference being that Angel is a textbook gourmand whereas Wish is a sweet oriental fragrance because of the presence of woody notes that also give it a bittersweet ,almost medicinal character. The latter is not necessarily a bad thing but it needs to be noted since Wish appears to be rumoured as a "funk-free" dupe to Angel. In other words, it might be cozy and sweet , but those who are looking for a warm crowd pleaser in the likes of LVEB will be dissapointed. The scent itself is hard to describe as I can hardly tell notes apart but the best parallel i can offer (may not be familiar to everyone), are the Pink rose/menthol "rendezvous" aromatic gummies , a Greek retro candy that served as a breath freshener. It's also worth mentioning that this is not a linear scent. It begins with a patchouli blast which soon settles sweet and then results in a very musky (strangely not listed) and woody drydown.
It took me a while to get warmed up to Wish and I do not regret buying it as I appreciate its quirky character, affordability and stunning bottle. Projection and sillage are adequate but you might need to overspray during winter.

A beautiful patchouli gourmand oriental. I understand the comparisons with TM Angel, as they're both sweet, heavy on the patch, 90s fragrance bombs with long note lists and come in blue bottles. Wish definitely falls into an almost edible category, it's a beautiful perfume that draws other people's attention and generates compliments and curiosity whenever I wear it. Quite versatile, appropriate to both, office meeting as well as a date night out. Great value for money. It shouldn't be, however, purchased as a blind buy/gift as It's not within the so called safe category. Wish is quite potent and has a unique quality to it, strong on coconut, caramel, osmanthus and heliotrope so may not be everyone's cuppa tea.
Beautiful and well pronounced, playful yet appropriate in formal settings.
I love you, Wish, you're my "here for the long haul" fragrance.

Gorgeous. Not an Angel dupe.

Sorry, it is very distinct from Angel. It certainly lacks the patchouli blast you get from Angel for women.

Chopard Wish is classy and seductive. Please note the honeysuckle. That really sets this one apart.

Madrona 02/23/16 14:50

I feel like the only person on this site who has never even smelled Angel, so I cannot say anything about the supposed similarity to said perfume. What I can say is that Wish is an extremely pleasant scent on my skin, there is not a single offensive quality about it. The listed notes seem to include everything but the kitchen sink and it works for me. Gourmand without being over-the-top sweet. Lovely.

EDIT: After smelling both Angel EdP and EdT on my skin, I can say that this is infinitely more wearable and way less polarizing. The patchouli note is considerably smaller in this one compared to Angel, so if Angel is too hardcore for you, don't be scared to try Wish.

EDIT 2: I applied Wish liberally before going to bed last night and put Lolita Lempicka on this morning. I subsequently headed to the gym, and as I was working out, a familiar smell started making its way into my nostrils... Angel EdP. It has been weeks since I used up my sample of Angel, so I thought I'd share this curious incident.

EDIT 3: I just got a whole big 75 ml thing of this as I have almost used up the 5 ml mini the review was based on. The mini was definitely an older one, and it smells better than what comes out of my large bottle. I don't know if it is the age that has changed the scent or if there has been a reformulation since 1999, but the mini smells a bit better to my nose. Warmer and a bit sweeter, somehow. There is a somewhat unpleasant note that is not present in the old one, so I don't know...

EDIT 4 (last one, I promise): Three days after getting the fullsize bottle I compare my mini with it yet again and actually prefer what comes out of the big bottle?! What is going on? I guess this is more complex than I thought!

SailorV 09/28/19 13:27

A beautiful patchouli gourmand oriental. I understand the comparisons with TM Angel, as they're both sweet, heavy on the patch, 90s fragrance bombs with long note lists and come in blue bottles. But Wish is not an Angel dupe, it smells quite different: Smoother and easier to wear, without the dirtier notes that turns many people off of Angel. It's still an intense nighttime/winter fragrance and for sure not for those who only wear light skin scents, but much less polarizing.
Wish is a sparkling, magical clean patchouli with lush, syrupy fruits, understated floral notes and dripping caramel on a powdery base. Sensual, feminine and well-blended. It's the predecessor to many darker fruitchoulis like La Nuit Trésor or Jimmy Choo. If you like this kind of fragrance, don't miss out on Wish!
And don't be afraid of the highly voted milk note if that's not your thing, not only can't I smell any milk here, I also could not find an official source for a milk note in Wish.

I don't know why I only really tried this great classic for the first time last winter. It's so affordable nowadays, I will get a bottle asap.

i urge everyone who is thinking of purchasing this because they read it is a dupe for mugler angel not to bother. i made this mistake, (pre-loreal) angel being my favourite perfume of all time, and was bitterly disappointed. i have absolutely no idea what happened to all of the many promising listed notes apparently present in this perfume as all i smell is an underwhelming, extremely generic sugary sweet slightly white floral milky scent that lasts all of an hour at best. no caramel, no toffee, no fruits, no incense and ABSOLUTELY no patchouli! this couldn't smell any less similar to angel if it tried. silage is minimal and like i said, lasting power is a joke. there really is nothing more i can say about this perfume, the only word i can think of to best describe it is bland. 1/10.
